title: Inference workshop sprint notes + slides outline
content:
Context:
This is a working pack for a 2.5 hour customer workshop focused on validating an inference POC and surface-level deployment options (hosted / dedicated / private). Goal is to leave with a clear success criteria, a short test plan, a proposed topology, and next steps for a 4-week POC.

Attendees (expected):
- Customer: ML lead, infra eng, product PM (3)
- Redwood: Solutions Eng (1x facilitator), Infra Eng (1x technical), Product PM (optional)

Pre-work for customer (send 7 days ahead):
- Short form: model(s) they want to evaluate, expected peak qps, latency SLO (p50/p95), dataset size for eval (example 500 queries).
- Provide a lightweight network checklist for private options (open ports, VPN/VPC peering).
- Ask for 3 representative prompts and 2 failure examples.

Workshop agenda (150 minutes)
1) 00:00–00:10 — Kickoff / Outcomes (10m)
   - Quick intros, alignment on success criteria for the session
   - Share 3 target outcomes: (A) validated test plan, (B) recommended deployment topology and rough cost/frame, (C) agreed next steps + owners

2) 00:10–00:25 — Customer context walkthrough (15m)
   - Customer presents product use case, expected traffic shape, security constraints
   - Clarifying Qs from SE team

3) 00:25–00:45 — Model & workload mapping (20m)
   - Map expected prompts to model variants (size, quantization tradeoffs)
   - Rough throughput/latency expectations per model
   - Quick heuristic: latency-sensitive? low-token? prefer smaller quantized model + dedicated; batchable high-throughput? consider deduped caching + hosted/dedicated with batching

4) 00:45–01:25 — Hands-on demo / smoke tests (40m)
   - Run 10–15 representative prompts against baseline hosted endpoint (we provide)
   - Capture p50/p95, token counts, sample outputs stored to shared sheet
   - Facilitator notes: have a fallback set of prompts if customer samples noisy. If network private demo required — use recorded traces/slides instead

5) 01:25–01:40 — Break (15m)

6) 01:40–02:10 — Deployment topology review + tradeoffs (30m)
   - Present 3 recommended deployment patterns: hosted API (fastest), dedicated pool (predictable throughput), private VPC (isolated/compliant)
content_continued:
- For each: short bullets (security, latency, ops, cost rough order) and when we recommend it
   - Example: dedicated pool -> guaranteed throughput for sustained qps > 150, supports autoscaling and private networking via private deployments

7) 02:10–02:30 — POC success criteria & test plan (20m)
   - Define primary metric(s): e.g., p95 <= X ms for model A under Y qps for 95% of traffic; semantic correctness threshold via holdout prompts (e.g., pass rate >= 85%)
   - Define telemetry to collect: token counts, latency histograms, error rates, model version tags
   - Owners: who runs tests, who reviews outputs, cadence for sync (weekly)

8) 02:30–02:50 — Risks, open questions, and next steps (20m)
   - Capture unresolved items: data residency approvals, network creds, expected budget for reserved capacity
   - Agreement on immediate next steps: access grant, POC contract timeline, kickoff date for 4-week POC
   - Assign owners and target dates

Slide outline (15 slides max)
- Title slide: Customer name + workshop date + expected outcomes
- Slide 1: Workshop agenda + roles
- Slide 2: Customer context snapshot (product, traffic, constraints)
- Slide 3: Model candidates + quick tradeoffs table (latency/cost/quality)
- Slide 4: Baseline demo results (p50/p95, token stats)
- Slide 5: Typical failure modes observed (example prompts + outputs)
- Slide 6: Deployment options overview (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Slide 7: Topology sketches (network diagrams for each option)
- Slide 8: Cost and ops comparison (rough numbers, assumptions)
- Slide 9: POC test plan and pass/fail criteria
- Slide 10: Telemetry & dashboards we will provide (console snapshots mock)
- Slide 11: Rollout plan beyond POC (canary -> gradual -> full)
- Slide 12: Security & compliance checklist (KMS, audit logs, data flow)
- Slide 13: Risks & mitigation plan
- Slide 14: Next steps, owners, dates
- Slide 15: Appendix (sample curl calls, key config snippets)

Facilitator cheat notes (bullet list)
- Keep the workshop customer-led when possible — they know constraints best
- Timebox the demo heavily; if a run fails, capture logs and move on — don't get stuck
- Use the p95 latency as the single SLI during debate; translate to UX impact (typing lag, API budget)
- When recommending dedicated vs hosted, highlight three real tradeoff anchors: cost predictability, isolation, and latency tail control
- Bring up Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization) as levers rather than immediate changes

Interactive exercises (scripts)
- Exercise A: "Latency budget tradeoff" (10m) — show two model configs (fp16-16B vs 4-bit-quant-13B) with simulated numbers; customers pick which to prioritize and explain why
- Exercise B: "Failover storyboard" (10m) — draw a simple flow: region outage -> routing policy -> fallback model -> degraded SLA. Get agreement on fallbacks and notifications

POC proposal sketch (to be refined after workshop)
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Scope: 2 model variants, sustained load test up to agreed qps (example 200rps for 30s windows), functional correctness on 500 holdout prompts, integration test with customer sandbox environment
- Deliverables: weekly telemetry report, end-of-POC quality evaluation, proposed production topology and cost estimate
- Rough pricing note: assume hosted up to 50k tokens/day for exploratory -> nominal. Dedicated reserved capacity estimate provided if expected sustained qps > 100

Test plan specifics (example)
- Synthetic load: ramp to target qps, hold for 15 minutes, capture latency distribution and error rates
- Functional checks: run 500 holdout prompts, compute pass rate against rubric (semantic match + hallucination checks)
- Regression alerts: set baseline on Day 2; any >5% drift in pass rate triggers joint review

Troubleshooting checklist (quick)
- If p95 much higher than hosted baseline: check KV cache warm-up, batch size, sequence length outliers, GPU utilization
- If errors spike: examine model version mismatch, tokenization errors, rate-limiter configuration
- If outputs degrade: confirm input preprocessing and context window are identical to baseline runs

Open questions to resolve post-workshop (seed list)
- Customer legal sign-off timeline for private deployment
- Expected sustained qps and daily token volume (need exact numbers)
- Which internal teams will own infra network setup for private option

Notes-to-self (facilitator)
- Bring a pre-populated Google Sheet to log demo outputs (prompt, response, tokens, p50/p95)
- Record the screen for the demo run (customer permission)
- If customer asks for cost projection, use conservative assumptions and flag them as preliminary

Follow-up template to send within 24 hours:
- Subject: "[Customer] — Workshop recap & POC next steps"
- Body: 1) recap outcomes, 2) agreed success criteria, 3) POC sketch + owner assignments, 4) attachments: demo results sheet + slide pdf

Slack/GH/Jira references to include in final notes:
- Slack thread: #poc-customername (create)
- Jira epic: JIRA-POC-214 (sample)
- GH repo: redwood-inference/poc-starter (templates)

End of working pack.

-- Maya
Notes: keep lightweight; this doc intentionally mixes polished slide outline with messy facilitator bullets so we can iterate in the next edit.
